subject: Flagship deal: lifeboat for real-time model affinity feature
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0000
Subject: Flagship deal: lifeboat for real-time model affinity feature

Team —

Quick ask from Sales: Goliath Systems (see deal GOL-8932) is asking for a lightweight, supported way to route a subset of their traffic to a dedicated model variant based on tenant affinity and a short-lived routing token. This is a gating item for closing (~$2.1M ARR, expected close in two weeks if we can commit).

What we need for an MVP lifeboat (to unblock procurement and the execs):
- Config flag at customer-level to opt into "model affinity" routing
- Simple routing key / header (they can set) that pins requests to a dedicated variant for the session
- Telemetry indicating when pins are used + clear fallback behavior to current variant
- Canary control (10% traffic cap) and kill switch

I attached a short requirements doc (mop_up_requirements.pdf) and the current term sheet (goliath-term-sheet.pdf). Can Product/Eng confirm whether we can scope this as a ~2-week delivery (small, temporary change) or if this is a larger effort? If we cannot commit to a small lifeboat, Sales needs an alternative we can point to in procurement.

Timeline is tight: procurement signatures due by 2027-09-10. Please reply with ETA and any blockers — we need a yes/no quickly.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: mop_up_requirements.pdf (11 pages, spec summary), goliath-term-sheet.pdf (redacted)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 16:04:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Flagship deal: lifeboat for real-time model affinity feature

Irene — thanks for the detail and the attachments. A few clarifying Qs before I commit this to the roadmap:

1) Acceptance criteria: what does "success" look like for Goliath at sign-off? (e.g., routed traffic percentage, latency delta tolerances, specific audit logs)
2) SLA expectations: will they need lower p99 or dedicated capacity guarantees once pinned?
3) Rollout: do they require an immediate tenant-level toggle in Console or will a server-side opt-in token suffice for now?

Operational concerns: routing pins that create hard affinity can increase KV cache pressure and tail latency on some models. If Goliath expects heavy pinned traffic we may need to reserve capacity or provide guidance on model quantization/instance sizing.

Possible lower-effort alternative: we could implement an "opt-in fallback" where pinned traffic is directed to an existing high-throughput variant with a best-effort affinity (no hard per-session pin). This reduces complexity at the cost of deterministic affinity. Would that be acceptable as an interim?

If Product signs off on minimal scope (flag + header + telemetry + 10% canary + kill switch), Eng should be able to prototype an approach next sprint and deliver a controlled canary in ~2–3 weeks. Dev — any initial thoughts?

—Ben
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@goliath.com>, Alex Romero <alex.romero@goliath.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 09:18:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Flagship deal: lifeboat for real-time model affinity feature

Ben — thanks. To answer:
- Success at sign-off: Goliath needs deterministic session affinity for the pinned calls during the pilot window (they care about consistency for multi-turn flows). They will accept up to +10ms p99 latency delta; beyond that procurement will push back.
- SLA: they are not asking for a long-term dedicated capacity SLA for the pilot; they want the ability to pin a subset of sessions and measure. Long-term SLA will be discussed later in the contract.
- Rollout: a server-side token header controlled by their integration will work for the pilot; Console toggle is nice-to-have but not required for initial close.

We can accept the "opt-in fallback" only if it's clearly marked as non-deterministic in the pilot docs — Goliath's success criteria require deterministic behavior. So we need the MVP to guarantee per-session pinning.

Procurement timeline: they need our commitment for this capability by COB 2027-09-03 to include in the negotiating addendum. HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/8932. Term sheet attached.

I can ask Goliath to accept a 10% canary and explicit rollback window. Please escalate if we need product approval.

—Irene

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 17:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Flagship deal: lifeboat for real-time model affinity feature

Thanks for the context. Engineering take (high level):

- Implementation plan (MVP lifeboat):
  1) Add a small routing hook that accepts a customer header (e.g., X-Goliath-Pin) and records a short-lived pin mapping in a lightweight in-memory map with TTL.
  2) At request time consult pin map before normal routing; if present, route to pinned variant; otherwise follow existing routing rules.
  3) Emit telemetry events (pin.created, pin.used, pin.expired) and a short trace id for debugging.
  4) Add a feature flag to enable/disable at tenant level and a global kill switch.

- Risks and mitigations:
  * KV cache pressure: limit pin TTL (e.g., 5–10 minutes) and enforce rate-limits per-tenant.
  * Determinism: ensure pin-map is consistent on per-instance basis for canary (we can run canary on a single pool to avoid cross-instance skew).
  * Perf: benchmark p50/p95 impact in staging; expected +2–8ms p95 depending on model size.

- ETA: If Product agrees to the constrained scope above, Eng can deliver a tested canary in ~12 business days (3 sprints of focused work with a small cross-functional team). That meets procurement if we start immediately. If Product requests a Console UI or long-lived persistence for pins, add +2–3 weeks.

Next steps: Ben/Marissa, can you confirm acceptance criteria and sign off on the constrained scope within 24h? If yes, Eng will raise JIRA-INF-4123 and schedule perf tests; Product please create the rollout checklist and canary plan.

—Dev Patel
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
